title: Causality Guided Disentanglement for Cross-Platform Hate Speech Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model generalization across distribution shifts by training on one source platform's dataset (Gab, Reddit, Twitter, or YouTube) and testing on unseen target platforms using macro-F1 scores.

Modeling race as a discrete platform-dependent target variable in a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) disentanglement framework to prevent spurious correlations with platform-specific racial identity words.
Modeling religion as a discrete target variable in a causal disentanglement framework to isolate religious identity representations from invariant hate speech features.
Modeling gender as a discrete target variable in a VAE disentanglement framework to separate gender identity representations from platform-independent causal hate features.
Modeling sexual preference as a discrete target variable to decouple sexual orientation identity terms from generalized hate speech predictions.
Including nationality in the discrete latent variable for platform-dependent features to prevent over-reliance on national identity words during hate speech detection.
Including immigration status as a target class in the disentanglement module to separate immigration-related identity representations from invariant causal hate features.
Categorizing ableness/disability as a discrete platform-dependent target variable to prevent the model from forming biases against disability-related identity terms.
Categorizing class as a discrete platform-dependent target variable in the VAE disentanglement module to separate socioeconomic identity features from the invariant hate speech representation.
